text:
sara_support: Hey @channel — we're seeing a large spike of 503s from hosted-prod between ~11:22-11:35 UTC. Multiple customers reporting timeouts and inference failures. Error looks like upstream worker crash (segfault / OOM). Investigating now.

michael_sre: +1 seeing the 503s in the gateway dashboard. QPS spiked by ~2.4x and error rate to 18%. Traces point to upstream inference runners in pool infer-pool-7.

anya_infra: I pulled node logs. There's a pattern: repeated CUDA OOM followed by runner process exit. Example from node-17: 
```
[2026-03-17T11:24:01Z] inference-runner[pid=4312]: GPU OOM allocating 3.2GB for KV cache
[2026-03-17T11:24:01Z] inference-runner[pid=4312]: runtime: fatal signal SIGSEGV
[2026-03-17T11:24:01Z] kernel: NVRM: GPU at fault: GPU 0: GPU HANG
```
Looks like large sequence lengths + batching caused unexpected memory blowups.

devon_ml: Which model variant was serving? Any quantization changes recently?

anya_infra: Most requests were to redwood-internal/v2-13b-q4a. No recent quantization deploys in the last 48h. There was a runtime packaging change rolled out 2h prior (inference-runtime 8.3.1).

michael_sre: We should confirm if 8.3.1 introduced any allocator changes. For triage: can we repro locally by sending long prompts with high batch size to a single GPU runner?

devon_ml: Repro attempt: sending 8 requests concurrently with sequence length ~4096 + sampling results in KV cache growth to ~11GB then OOM on 24GB card if other processes present. Sending single long request is fine; it's the combination of long seq + concurrency.

lee_cs: Affected customers: corp-acme and travelmate reported timeouts and escalated to CS. corp-acme's request logs show prompt length ~3800 tokens + images (they're using multimodal prep). Travelmate had a sudden QPS increase after bulk ingestion.

anya_infra: Quick mitigation options:
- throttle per-request max tokens for hosted tier to 2048 (config change)
- temporarily reduce max concurrent in-flight per-runner to 6
- route heavy requests to dedicated nodes with bigger GPU memory (if available)
- rollback runtime 8.3.1 to 8.3.0 on the pool

michael_sre: I'm starting an emergency canary rollback of inference-runtime 8.3.1 on infer-pool-7 to 8.3.0 for 10% of traffic. deploy-bot: can you initiate a rollback ticket?
deploy-bot: Rollback request created: RB-2026-311. Rolling back 10% of infer-pool-7 to inference-runtime 8.3.0 now. Will monitor for 5 min.

anya_infra: Rolling a config to set per-request token cap to 2048 for hosted-prod (hotfix). Applying to API gateway now.

michael_sre: Added temporary routing rule: requests with tokens>2048 are routed to fallback queue and get 429 with retry-after; we'll communicate to CS.

devon_ml: Logged a repro script in the infra repo (link: https://git.internal/repro/gpu-oom-surge). Script sends concurrent long prompts to replicate KV growth. Use `EXPORT SAMPLES=8` and `SEQLEN=4096` to reproduce.

anya_infra: dmesg snippet from node-17: 
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:00:1f): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12345.679012] kernel: oid 0x7f -> segfault at 0x00000000 ip 0x7f6b9f... sp 0x7ffd...
```
Also container runtime logs show repeated `OOMKilled` followed by k8s backoff restarts.

michael_sre: Observed fallback routing kick-in; error rate dropping from 18% -> 7% after throttle. Rolling back the runtime canary now shows initial signs of improved stability in canary nodes.

devon_ml: Hypothesis: runtime 8.3.1 changed KV prefetch heuristics causing larger memory reservation under concurrent streams and a race leading to segfault during memcpy. We'll bisect the allocator change.

anya_infra: For immediate ops: I've drained the most affected nodes and cordoned node-17. Scheduling a live core dump collection for one crashed pod (will attach to ticket RB-2026-311). Please avoid restarting pod until we capture core.

lee_cs: Notifying corp-acme and travelmate with interim mitigation: token cap + expected retry behavior. CS will offer credits if they saw >5% failed requests in last hour.

michael_sre: Action items:
- devon_ml to bisect runtime change and confirm allocator regression (OWNER: devon_ml)
- anya_infra to collect core dump + kernel logs and escalate to driver team (OWNER: anya_infra)
- michael_sre to monitor canary rollback and hold until 30m stable (OWNER: michael_sre)
- sara_support/lee_cs to notify impacted customers and track credit requests (OWNER: lee_cs)

anya_infra: Collected core and uploaded to internal bucket: gs://redwood-debug/rb-2026-311/node-17-core.tar.gz. Added notes on env: CUDA 12.2, driver 535.86, kernel 5.15. Memory map included.

devon_ml: Bisect result so far: reverting allocator patch CL-4789 removes OOM in our repro harness. Filing a PR to revert and test.

michael_sre: Canary rollback stable for 20m. Error rate on canary nodes back to baseline. Proceeding to roll the rest of infer-pool-7 back to 8.3.0.

deploy-bot: Rollback completed for infer-pool-7: all nodes on 8.3.0. Tickets closed: RB-2026-311.

anya_infra: Post-rollback, nodes still show a couple of segfaults but lower rate — likely memory fragmentation remnants. Scheduling a follow-up kernel/driver patch window next week.

devon_ml: Merged revert PR, will add stricter mem-accounting tests to prevent regression.

lee_cs: Corp-acme and travelmate updated. Offering 10% credits and follow-up postmortem.

michael_sre: Summary for postmortem: cause = allocator heuristic change in 8.3.1 that increased reservation under concurrent long-seq workloads leading to GPU OOM and subsequent segfaults; impact = hosted 503 spike affecting several customers; mitigations = rollback runtime, token caps, routing throttles, drained nodes; next steps = revert code, add tests, driver/kernel patch window.

sara_support: Thanks team. I'll open the incident PM and attach the core + repro steps. Closing Slack thread once postmortem draft is ready. :thumbsup:
